objectives: This review aimed to provide an integrated synthesis bridging mechanistic evidence, especially anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, with clinical outcomes such as mortality and arrhythmias for L-carnitine supplementation in coronary artery disease, while critically appraising inconsistencies such as heart failure and reinfarction findings.
inclusion_criteria: This review considered peer-reviewed studies of L-carnitine supplementation in subjects with coronary artery disease across predefined designs, including preclinical animal studies, case reports, cross-sectional studies, observational studies, retrospective analyses, randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses. Included studies investigated effects on cardiac function, oxidative stress, inflammation, and/or mortality in CAD patients.
exclusion_criteria: This review excluded papers that did not fit the scope of the review and those not published in English or without an available English translation.
pmid_query: PubMed and Google Scholar were searched through July 13, 2025 using the keywords L-carnitine, L-carnitine supplementation, coronary artery disease, and ischemic heart disease in varied ways with AND as the search operator; cited-reference searching was also performed.
selection_evidence: Results state that after screening and duplicate removal the search produced 21 results, PRISMA Figure 1 reports studies included in the final review (n = 21), and Table 1 Summary of the enrolled trials (n = 21) lists the included records in author-year form. The manuscript uses author-year in-text citations and an alphabetical reference list, so exact numbered references are not available.
notes:
The included records are heterogeneous and comprise 11 clinical trials/RCTs, 2 preclinical animal studies, and 8 review/meta-analysis articles. The Nachvak trial is cited in Table 1 as 2020, but the RIS export lists 2023 metadata with DOI 10.1080/13813455.2020.1797102. For Khedr et al. 2022, the included record is the cardiotoxicity paper in Cardiovascular Toxicology, not the unrelated testicular-toxicity paper.

Manual update note: Manual review confirmed the remaining unresolved study is not indexed in PubMed; gold_pmids now reflect only OK rows.
